model: Takeover scheme: deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting over a standalone Energy-only owner-FCF DCF (engine route)

equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR lines 9461/9469: 158,980 assets less 49,608 liabilities (GBP thousands)

equity_bridge.item: Nexora (DCC Technology) sale -- estimated net proceeds; segment flows excluded from the model

Segment book net assets were 789 (assets 1,185.0 less liabilities 395.9, lines 9457/9465), so a further loss on disposal is likely but is non-cash.

Equity accounted investments at book (income excluded from EBITDA)
Non-controlling interests -- 40% minority in DCC Holding Denmark A/S at ~11x its GBP14.9m profit share
equity_bridge.note: Note 4.4; book value 102.7 is the floor

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: DCC Energy organic growth: AOP +1.8% FY2025 and +1.3% FY2026 on volumes of -3.1% with pence-per-litre gross margin up 11% (13.6p vs 12.2p); total Energy AOP +3.5% FY2026 including bolt-ons. 2.0% nominal revenue growth is the organic path the pre-acquisition FCF can be credited with.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every group-level CAGR above is polluted by the portfolio transformation and is NOT a growth signal: revenue 3-yr is negative because Healthcare, Exertis France/Iberia and Info Tech were divested; statutory EPS collapsed to 14.12p in FY2026 on the 258.7 discontinued-operations loss (continuing adjusted EPS was 438.1p, +9.9%); equity fell on the GBP700m buyback and divestment write-downs; the owner-FCF series mixes the old and new perimeters. Like-for-like Energy-only history exists for two years only (FY2025 restated vs FY2026).
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs computed on the group Metrics.csv: revenue FY2021 13,412.5 -> FY2026 15,441.9 (5y), FY2023 22,204.8 -> FY2026 (3y); statutory EPS 2.966 -> 0.141 (5y), 3.38 -> 0.141 (3y); shareholders' equity 2,647.4 -> 2,260.9 (5y), 2,978.1 -> 2,260.9 (3y); owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC, no interest strip) 558.8 -> 459.6 (5y), 420.3 -> 459.6 (3y). SBC is immaterial (0.02-0.05% of revenue throughout) so owner and reported FCF CAGRs are the same.

scenario_narratives.base: Standalone DCC Energy (deal-breaks leg): 2% nominal revenue growth, EBITDA margin 5.9% -> 6.2% over ten years (AOP ~3%/yr), capex ~1.2% of revenue, 23% cash tax, lease cash charged inside EBITDA (treatment B), 8% GBP WACC, terminal min(Gordon 2%, 15x FCF). Nexora enters as ~GBP500m of net sale proceeds in the bridge. Answers 'what is the business worth if the consortium walks?'
scenario_narratives.bull: Standalone upside: organic delivery toward the 2030 doubling ambition -- CEE liquid gas, bioLPG/HVO, Energy Services recovery, Mobility services -- gives revenue +4% then +3% and EBITDA margin to 6.8% (AOP ~6%/yr), terminal 16x. Approximately the dissenting shareholders' case.
scenario_narratives.bear: Standalone downside: scheme fails into a soft market -- volumes -3%/yr, Energy Services losses persist, working-capital tailwind reverses, margin erodes to 5.4%, terminal 12x; the stock reverts toward its undisturbed ~5,380p.

valuation_philosophy.summary: DCC Energy is a live, shareholder-approved take-private, so the valuation is an event-weighted one: P(complete) x PV(6,525p cash + ~42p Nexora-linked payment, expected Q1 2027) plus P(break) x standalone intrinsic value. The standalone leg is an owner-FCF DCF of DCC Energy alone (Solutions + Mobility), built from FY2026 segment components with leases charged as operating cost, SBC expensed (immaterial), NCI and deferred consideration charged once in the bridge, and Nexora's US$725m sale added as net proceeds rather than modelled as a flow. The engine's three scenarios and their weights describe the deal-breaks world only; `takeover.deal_weighted_iv` is the figure a holder today should compare with the price, and `probability_weighted.weighted_iv` is the answer to 'was 6,525p a fair price?'. Statutory FY2026 profit (13.4 after the 258.7 discontinued loss) and the group-level ten-year history are not inputs: the perimeter changed too much.
key_risks_to_valuation: Completion risk: Irish High Court sanction and remaining regulatory clearances; the scheme passed with only 78.09% against a 75% threshold and large holders argued publicly the price is too low -- a break sends the stock toward its ~5,380p undisturbed level, not toward standalone IV

Nexora contingent payment: the c.42p estimate depends on the Transaction Agreement's net-proceeds deductions and the undisclosed hurdle; it could settle lower or at zero if the Nexora sale fails to complete by 31 July 2027
Timing: each quarter of delay beyond Q1 2027 costs ~1pp of annualised return on the merger-arb spread

Standalone leg: DCC Energy's lease, ROU-depreciation and SBC splits by segment are estimated at ~90% of continuing totals; NCI fair value (GBP165m) and Nexora net proceeds (GBP500m of GBP548m gross) are judgments
Standalone leg: terminal multiple -- DCC never sustainably traded at the 15x FCF cap used in the base; the consortium is paying ~16x, which is itself the re-rating the public market never granted
FX: 77% of Energy AOP is earned outside sterling (EUR, USD, NOK/SEK) and is unhedged in translation; a stronger pound lowers every GBP flow
Working capital: the FY2026 71.4 inflow was commodity-price driven and is modelled as non-recurring (wc_capture 0); a sharp fall in LPG/fuel prices would make it an outflow

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (LSE regular close); 52-week range 4,188-6,740p; prior close 6,435p
data_sources.financials: DCC.L_Annual_FY2026.txt (segment note 2.1 lines 9399-9553; income statement 8881-8904; cash flow 9109-9159; finance costs note 2.6 line 9938; leases 11315-11330; net debt/capital structure 12505-12530; notes 3.5, 4.1, 4.4), DCC.L_Metrics.csv (22 periods FY2016-FY2026), DCC.L_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt (Q3 FY2026 trading statement, 2026-02-04)
data_sources.qualitative: DCC.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10); Rule 2.7 announcement 'Recommended Acquisition of DCC Energy plc' 2026-07-27 (Investegate RNS 9687627) for offer terms, 86,243,641 fully-diluted count, Q1-2027 expected effective date, 31 July 2027 Technology Disposal long-stop; RNS 'Nexora Sale and Additional Consideration Estimate' 2026-10-09 and Reuters/RTE/Peel Hunt coverage for US$725m and the c.42p estimate; scheme meeting result 2026-09-18 (78.09%) per Irish Independent/RTE

takeover.status: Recommended cash acquisition by Dragon Bidco (Energy Capital Partners / KKR) under an Irish scheme of arrangement; Rule 2.7 announced 2026-07-27; scheme approved by shareholders 2026-09-18 (78.09% of scheme shares voted in favour vs 75% threshold); Irish High Court sanction and regulatory clearances outstanding; expected to become effective Q1 2027.

offer_terms.final_dividend_note: FY2026 final, paid 2026-07-23 to holders on the register 2026-05-29 -- counted in the headline 6,672.22p/GBP5.75bn but NOT forward value for a buyer today
offer_terms.technology_disposal_note: Linear between an undisclosed hurdle and US$800m of Nexora net proceeds; long-stop 31 July 2027. Nexora agreed sold to One Equity Partners for US$725m on 2026-10-09; company RNS 'Nexora Sale and Additional Consideration Estimate' and Peel Hunt put the payment at c.42p.

deal_completes.discount_rate_note: Conditional on completion the cash is near-certain and ~5 months away, so it is discounted at roughly the 1-year gilt yield; completion risk is carried in the probability, not the rate (risk charged once).

deal_breaks.undisturbed_note: Implied by the 24% premium of 6,672.22p (base + dividend) stated in the Rule 2.7; where the stock would likely trade on a break, versus the DCF's standalone intrinsic value.

takeover.deal_weighted_iv_note: P(complete) x PV(6,567p) + P(break) x standalone weighted IV (probability_weighted.weighted_iv). This is the value a holder today should compare with current_price; probability_weighted.weighted_iv is the standalone (deal-breaks) value and answers whether the offer is fair.
takeover.deal_weighted_entry_price_note: P(complete) x 15%-IRR entry on the consideration + P(break) x standalone weighted 15%-hurdle entry price.
takeover.market_implied_note: Solving price = p x PV(consideration) + (1-p) x undisturbed price. The market prices ~97% completion; the house 92% is deliberately more cautious because of the narrow 78% vote, vocal dissenting holders and multi-jurisdiction clearances still outstanding.
takeover.probability_rationale: 92% complete / 8% break: scheme already approved by shareholders, financing committed, no material horizontal antitrust overlap between the consortium's portfolios and off-grid LPG/fuels distribution, but Irish High Court sanction, UK/EU/US clearances and FDI reviews remain, and the vote margin was unusually thin for a recommended deal.

offer_vs_standalone.note: The house standalone value sits ~11% above the expected consideration -- directionally the dissenters' point -- but the bear leg (4,882p) and DCC's never-re-rated history are why a 6,567p cash certainty was accepted.

inputs.base_revenue_note: DCC Energy segment revenue FY2026 (DCC.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:9408, GBP thousands 12,990,355). The DCC Technology / Nexora segment (revenue 2,451.5, AOP 79.8) is EXCLUDED from the flows because it was sold for US$725m on 2026-10-09; its value enters the equity bridge as net proceeds instead. FY2025 restated Energy revenue was 13,366.6 (-2.8%, commodity-price driven; volumes -3.1%).
inputs.share_count_basis: 87,609,229 issued less 2,185,094 treasury = 85,424,135 at 31 March 2026 (note 4.1, line 12017) plus 0.249m dilutive options/awards from the diluted-EPS table (note 2.11, line 10324) = 85.67m. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The Rule 2.7 announcement uses 86.24m 'issued and to be issued' (adds a maximum 819,506 shares under share plans, most of which vest on change of control); that larger count is used for the per-share deal arithmetic in the takeover block, not for the standalone DCF. The FY2026 GBP700m buyback (13,724,675 shares) is complete; no repurchases since (offer period).
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings 1,653.7 non-current + 231.7 current = 1,885.5 (line 9467) less cash and short-term deposits 1,085.6 (line 9156) = 799.8 gross. The company's own 'net debt excluding lease creditors' is 690.5 (line 12522) because it nets the 109.4 net derivative asset (cross-currency swaps hedging the US private placement notes: 159.0 assets less 49.6 liabilities, lines 9461/9469); that 109.4 is added back as an equity_bridge item so the bridge ties to the company figure. Lease creditors (389.8) are deliberately EXCLUDED from net debt: lease treatment (B), see lease_treatment.
inputs.sbc_source: Group cash flow note 5.3 'Share based payment expense (note 2.4)' 3,432 GBP thousands FY2026 (line 9728; 7,544 FY2025). No cash tax on net-share settlement is disclosed, so sbc_incl_equity_taxes = sbc. The 1,785 at line 12474 is the parent-company-only charge and is not used.
inputs.last_fcf_note: reported_fcf = net cash from operating activities 672.5 less purchase of PPE 209.5 (lines 9119, 9130) = 463.0 for the whole group (continuing plus the Healthcare/Info Tech stubs to their disposal dates). Owner FCF = 463.0 - 3.4 SBC - 0 interest income = 459.6. This is a record anchor only: it is after interest paid (96.1) and BEFORE the 86.6 lease principal (treatment B deducts the full 92.3 continuing lease payment inside EBITDA), and it includes a 71.4 working-capital inflow the company itself says would reverse if commodity prices normalise. The engine projects from the Energy-only component build below, whose year-1 unlevered owner FCF is ~GBP395-400m (3.0% of revenue).
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income 13.3 (8.9 on deposits) is NOT stripped: DCC is a net-debt company (690.5 company basis), so the interest-income rule (net cash > 1x FCF) does not apply. The engine's flows are unlevered, so neither interest income nor the 104.8 finance cost sits in the projections; both are captured through net debt in the bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: GBP700.0m share buyback/tender in FY2026 financing activities (line 9143), funded from Healthcare disposal proceeds; 13.72m shares cancelled at an average ~GBP51.0. A repurchaser, so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP (millions). LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP), so fx_rate 100 converts model GBP per share to quote GBp. No dual listing to parity-check; the Rule 2.7 offer itself is denominated in pence (6,525p), which anchors the quote basis. US$725m Nexora proceeds converted at GBPUSD 1.3233 (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-10-09T21:29Z).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T15:36:23Z (LSE regular close; today's session 2026-10-10 not yet closed at build time)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the flows' currency: UK 10y gilt ~4.5% risk-free + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.9 = ~9.0% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt 4.4% (83.6 interest on ~1,886 gross debt, 75% fixed, BBB) = ~3.4% after tax; weights ~88% equity / 12% debt at a ~GBP5.5bn market cap and 0.7bn net debt -> WACC ~8.3%, rounded to 8.0%. The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, weather, Energy Services execution and decarbonisation risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost, matching DCC's own free-cash-flow definition (which deducts 'repayment of lease creditors' 100.6). The full continuing lease payment on capitalised right-of-use assets (92.3 = 86.6 principal in financing + ~13.0 lease interest in finance costs, lines 11322/9950) is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path, scaled to DCC Energy (~90% share, ~83 = 0.64% of Energy revenue). Lease creditors (389.8) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt, and da_pct_path is depreciation EXCLUDING right-of-use assets (Energy 139.2, line 9531) so the lease is not charged twice. Short-term/variable lease cash (64.2) is already inside operating costs and AOP.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: NCI is the 40% minority in DCC Holding Denmark A/S (note 4.4), book GBP102.7m, GBP14.9m/yr profit share (3.9% of FY2026 attributable adjusted profit). The flows are modelled 100% consolidated and the NCI stock is deducted at an estimated GBP165m (~11x its profit share; the book value materially understates a profitable Danish LPG minority). Associates (79.2, mainly the retained minority in the Hong Kong & Macau liquid gas business, 4.6 profit share) are the mirror case: their income is outside EBITDA, so the asset is added at book.
inputs.notes: MODEL: live takeover -- the routing table's 'Live takeover, scheme, strategic review' row, implemented as a deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting over a standalone owner-FCF DCF (engine route). On 27 July 2026 the board agreed a recommended cash acquisition by Dragon Bidco (Energy Capital Partners / KKR) under an Irish scheme of arrangement: 6,525p Base Consideration per share, plus the 147.22p FY2026 final dividend (ALREADY PAID 23 July 2026, so not forward value), plus a Technology Disposal Additional Consideration of up to 125p linked to the Nexora sale net proceeds (linear between an undisclosed hurdle and US$800m; long-stop 31 July 2027). Shareholders approved the scheme on 18 September 2026 (78.09% of scheme shares voted in favour, a narrow margin against a 75% threshold); remaining conditions are Irish High Court sanction and regulatory clearances; completion expected Q1 2027. On 9 October 2026 DCC Energy agreed to sell Nexora to One Equity Partners for US$725m and estimated the additional consideration at c.42p per share, so the expected forward consideration is 6,567p. THE THREE ENGINE SCENARIOS ARE THE DEAL-BREAKS (STANDALONE) WORLD ONLY, and their weights are conditional on the deal failing. The deal-completes leg and the deal-weighted value are in the top-level `takeover` block; `probability_weighted.weighted_iv` is the STANDALONE value and answers 'is the offer fair?', while `takeover.deal_weighted_iv` is what a holder today should compare with the price. Standalone basis: DCC Energy only (Solutions + Mobility), FY2026 segment actuals, Nexora in the bridge as net proceeds. Pending UGI Central/Eastern European liquid gas acquisitions (Poland, Hungary, Czechia, Slovakia; agreed January 2026, completing Q2 FY2027, consideration within the GBP112.4m committed) are ignored as roughly value-neutral at acquisition multiples. Working capital: DCC runs a negative working-capital model (0.4 days of sales at March 2026) so wc_capture is set to 0; the FY2026 71.4 inflow was commodity-price driven and management expects it to reverse. SBC-near-zero market: house and street bases nearly coincide (SBC 0.026% of revenue); band_position is reported but is close to degenerate. FY2026 statutory attributable profit of 13.4 (after a 258.7 loss on discontinued operations) is NOT the earnings base; continuing adjusted EPS 438.1p and Energy AOP 554.2 are.

bear.narrative: Deal-breaks standalone, downside axis: the scheme fails (court or regulatory) into a weaker backdrop -- mild winters and electrification cut volumes 3%/yr, Energy Services stays loss-making, the FY2026 working-capital inflow reverses as commodity prices normalise, and per-litre margin gains stall. Revenue flat, EBITDA margin erodes to 5.4%, terminal 12x FCF (DCC's own chronic low-multiple history: the board conceded it 'has not sustainably re-rated in the public markets'). Undisturbed price before the approach was ~5,380p.

base.ebitda_margin_note: FY2026 Energy: AOP 554.2 + non-ROU depreciation 139.2 + ~70 ROU depreciation (90% of continuing 78.1) = ~763 pre-IFRS16-lease EBITDA = 5.88% of 12,990; drifts +5bp/yr to 6.2% on per-litre margin and procurement synergies, i.e. AOP growth ~3%/yr with revenue +2%. Lease cost 0.64% then deducted inside EBIT. Year-1 EBIT ~538 ties to Energy AOP 554.2 less ~12 lease interest.
base.capex_note: Energy net capex 151.8 (gross additions 195.1 less disposal proceeds, line 1881/9515) = 1.17% of revenue; 1.20% holds capex ~12% above non-ROU depreciation, as in FY2026 (company: net capex exceeded depreciation by 11.5 group-wide).
base.tax_note: Continuing pre-exceptional P&L tax 95.7 on PBT 445.9 = 21.5%; cash tax paid 127.6 includes discontinued stubs. 23% on unlevered EBIT is above the 21.9% effective rate because the engine taxes EBIT before the ~GBP90m deductible interest.
base.narrative: Deal-breaks standalone: DCC Energy runs as a focused LPG/fuels/Mobility distributor. Volumes drift down 1-3%/yr but pence-per-litre margin, bolt-on procurement synergies and Mobility non-fuel services lift AOP ~3%/yr. Revenue grows 2% nominal (commodity-price neutral), EBITDA margin 5.9% -> 6.2%, capex ~1.2% of revenue, 23% cash tax, no working-capital tailwind. Terminal 15x FCF cap vs ~16x the consortium is paying.

bull.narrative: Deal-breaks standalone, upside axis: the 2030 ambition to double Energy AOP is partly delivered organically -- Central/Eastern European liquid gas entry and bioLPG/HVO hold volumes flat, Energy Services recovers from its FY2026 trough (AOP 15.7 vs 48.3), Mobility non-fuel gross profit keeps compounding at double digits. Revenue +4% then +3%, EBITDA margin to 6.8%, AOP ~6%/yr. This is roughly what the dissenting holders (Fidelity, Aviva, founder Jim Flavin at ~GBP100/share) argued the business is worth; the market never paid it.

entry_price.method: Standalone engine entry prices are the 15%-IRR buy-below prices for the deal-breaks world (terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle). For the deal-completes leg the 15% hurdle entry price is the expected 6,567p consideration discounted at 15% over ~0.39 years to the expected Q1-2027 close = ~6,218p; see takeover.deal_completes_entry_price_15pct and takeover.deal_weighted_entry_price.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: These weights are CONDITIONAL ON THE DEAL BREAKING; the completion probability itself lives in the `takeover` block. Bear raised from the 15% default to 30% because a broken scheme (court refusal, regulatory block, or a consortium exit) would almost certainly coincide with an adverse backdrop and management distraction, and DCC's own board conceded the standalone equity 'has not sustainably re-rated'. Bull cut to 20%: the organic-doubling case needs CEE integration, an Energy Services recovery and flat volumes to all come through at once -- three independent things.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
